bio: Michelle Paty was a nurse and nurse practitioner in the cardiac ICU before she moved into aesthetics in 2019. Her first job trained her for four days, then put her on cheek and jawline filler with no mentor in the state. She learned as she went.

In 2022 she opened Skin Den in a 100 square foot room in Denver, hiring for energy as much as skill. Within months it became Preva, for preventative aesthetics, a name that could travel. Today her injectors train for at least two to three months before their first basic treatments, and every opening draws more than 300 applications.

traits.label: Train longer than the industry does.
traits.line: “This industry is really an art, and there's a lot to it.”

traits.label: One standard, everywhere.
traits.line: “If you have a high standard, you're gonna have a high standard across the board.”

traits.label: Hire for energy.
traits.line: “I think the people were the biggest thing. So it was about who I was hiring.”

quotes.text: I felt like they had a firm direction. They had very high standards, and it matched ours.
The parts that you love about Preva are not going to change. They're gonna get stronger. They're gonna get better.

milestones: Leaves the cardiac ICU for aesthetics. Four days of training, no mentor in the state.
Opens Skin Den in a 100 square foot room in Denver.
Renamed Preva, for preventative aesthetics. A name that could travel.
